newsitem.title: CHINA: China sentences U.S. businessman to 10 years.
newsitem.headline: China sentences U.S. businessman to 10 years.

text.p: A Chinese court sentenced U.S. businessman William Ping Chen on Monday to 10 years in jail for smuggling, fined him 500,000 yuan ($60,000) and ordered him to be deported, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Chen had confessed to the charges of smuggling banned goods, including 238 tons of garbage and a small amount of waste medical items between July and December 1995, Xinhua said.

The Shanghai Number One People's Intermediate Court sentenced Chen to 10 years in jail and ordered his expulsion from China after finding him guilty of smuggling "foreign garbage" for profit, it said.
It was not clear whether Chen was to be deported immediately after sentencing.

Chen, 56, who was arrested in June last year, was sentenced following an open hearing on Dec. 2 at which he was defended by two lawyers, Xinhua said. The hearing was attended by an official from the U.S. consulate in Shanghai, it said.

Chen had insisted on going ahead with the imports of banned waste items despite warnings from officials of the Shanghai municipal environmental protection burea and the Chinese partners in his Shanghai-based joint venture, it said.
His smuggling of banned goods "had caused serious damage to the environment," the court verdict said.
The court also ordered Chen to pay a fine of 500,000 yuan ($60,000), Xinhua said.
Chen's arrest followed a furore in China over alleged illegal imports of U.S. garbage masquerading as waste paper for recycling and which escalated last year into an issue of national pride.

His sentencing was the first in China of a U.S. citizen since human rights activist Harry Wu was detained in June 1995, convicted of spying and sentenced to 15 years in jail. He was deported to the United States within hours of his sentencing.
